findings.summary: crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: Part 3 refuses readings for every request-cited job with unlanded files, even when the reading relies on nothing from that job. Root-cause requests, including this one, will be refused routinely.
findings.evidence: `referenced_jobs` carries every job id written in the request (reading.rs:2343). Today these jobs are deliberately not checked: "jobs it cites as evidence (such as the introspections in a root-cause request) are shown to the reader, not checked" (reading.rs:510-512), and the doc comment at 2364-2367 says the same. Root-cause requests are generated automatically and cite rejected jobs whose candidate files never landed. This request cites six jobs. The accepted reading names only three of them in out_of_scope; 20261025-001236-brde, 20261026-145124-ssmw and 20261026-145955-s7e2 are missing. Under Part 3, the reading this job runs on would be refused unless those jobs have no added files. Citing a job is not relying on it. A rule that fires on every cited rejected job is a false-positive generator, and its only repair is boilerplate out_of_scope entries. That is the opposite of checking what the reading says exists. Fix: Start Part 3 from what the reading relies on, not from the request's citations. A cited or retried job's unlanded added or created files count only when the reading's own text names the job id, one of those paths, or a file stem of one. Reliance through a path or symbol without the id is already caught by Parts 1 and 2. Keep evidence-only citations unchecked, as reading.rs:510-512 does now. Add a test where a request cites a rejected job with unlanded files, the reading never mentions it, and the reading is accepted.

findings.summary: The symbol-shape rule still picks up brand words, environment-variable names and local bindings, and none of them is a definition in .rs.
findings.evidence: The CamelCase rule is "an internal lowercase-to-uppercase change" with at least 5 characters. That makes GitHub, JavaScript and PostgreSQL candidates, and GitHub is this project's host (system facts: `parse_remote` in gh.rs). UPPER_SNAKE environment-variable names appear in .rs only inside string literals, which `defines_symbol` skips. A survey naming a `let` binding such as `repo_files` (reading.rs:514) finds no item, field or variant definition. Each of these refuses a truthful survey and uses up the reader's one correction (`read_for`). Fix: For CamelCase and UPPER_SNAKE words, require a code marker: a backtick span, a `::` path, or a following `(`. Keep bare snake_case-with-underscore as a candidate. Alternatively, count `let <name>` and string-literal uses for UPPER_SNAKE. Add guard cases for `GitHub` and an environment-variable name in a survey.

findings.summary: Path tokens relative to a crate are silently unchecked, a narrowing D146 should state.
findings.evidence: Surveys often write paths like `src/reading.rs`. `src` is not a top-level directory, so these are dropped. Such a path to a missing file passes. Fix: Record this narrowing in D146 next to the plain-role-word narrowing, or resolve such a path when exactly one snapshot path ends with it.
findings.location: Plan Step 2 Part 1 (the first component must be a top-level directory of `files`)

summary: I checked the plan's code references with Read and Grep; I did not build or run anything. The plan is well grounded in the code. These exist where the plan says: `read_once` and its `check_reading_acceptance` call (reading.rs:499-529), `referenced_jobs` (2335), `unaccounted_files` (2472), `names_path_token` (2516), `check_boundary_and_repo_files` (2600), `replay_declaration` (3299), the `earlier()` and `files_at_head()` test helpers, `Git::cat_blobs` (athena-git lib.rs:856), `EarlierAttempt` with `changed_files` as `status path` (briefs.rs:1437), and the reader-level helpers in run_pin_tests.rs (`reader_edits`, `refusal_section`, the test at 1707). The demonstrations use real seams. The reader-level tests through `Athena::ask` would fail if the check were not wired into `read_once`, which answers the earlier wiring concern. Athena's finding that run_pin_tests.rs is not among the reading's deliverables is justified by that need and stays minor. One soundness problem needs a revision. Part 3 now checks every job the request cites, which reverses the code's deliberate rule that jobs cited as evidence are not checked. Root-cause requests cite several rejected jobs with unlanded files, so readings that rely on none of them would be refused. The reading this job runs on would itself fail, because it names only three of the six cited jobs in out_of_scope. Part 3 should start from what the reading itself names. Two smaller findings: the symbol-shape rule still flags brand words such as GitHub, environment-variable names and local bindings, and paths relative to a crate go unchecked without saying so.
